# Standard Streams and File Descriptors

Linux processes inherit three default file descriptors:
* `0`: `stdin` (Standard Input)
* `1`: `stdout` (Standard Output)
* `2`: `stderr` (Standard Error)

Custom descriptors (3 to 9) can be allocated for custom logging or teeing:

```bash
# Allocate FD 3 to write to a log file
exec 3> /var/log/custom-audit.log

# Write directly to FD 3
echo "Audit event at $(date)" >&3

# Close FD 3
exec 3>&-
```
